column1: # Selectors are semantic fallback policies, not an allowlist of resources or a
# resource-count cap. The daemon also discovers kernel-advertised selector choices
# and sysfs companion bounds, so newly exposed controls need not be listed here.
# Rows below provide known semantic ranges where Linux does not publish bounds.
# Virtual-memory controls (the runtime rejects values outside the selected policy range).
# Kernel scheduling controls; rows apply only where the running kernel exposes them.
# Per-device block queue controls. Each discovered queue is handled independently.
# Elevator tunables (sysfs.block.iosched). The set of attributes is discovered from
# /sys/block/<dev>/queue/iosched/, which exists only for the elevator the kernel
# currently runs. Bounds below are kernel-documented ranges; a live value outside
# them is never proposed for mutation.
# CPU governor tunables (sysfs.cpu.governor). Discovered only from the directory of
# the governor each policy is running now, e.g. policyN/schedutil/rate_limit_us.
